tagline: Back roads down to the lead mines on the New River.
intro: Out of Rural Retreat the country roads run through Speedwell and past Noble Furnace on Francis Mill Creek, where a steam-powered iron furnace with a stone stack once worked ore brought in by tramway. They reach the New River at Austinville.
Farther north a second set of roads, Fort Chiswell Road, Max Meadows Road and Peppers Ferry Road, runs from near Poplar Camp toward Wytheville.

moments.title: Rural Retreat
moments.text: A town by the railroad that began as Mount Airy, with a depot of that name, and changed it because too many other places were Mount Airy already.

moments.title: Austinville
moments.text: Built on Lead Mines, once the seat of a Fincastle County that took in all of present Kentucky, it is where Stephen F. Austin was born in 1793.

moments.title: Jackson Ferry Shot Tower
moments.text: Molten lead fell 150 feet here to become shot, down a 75-foot limestone tower on a cliff edge and a 75-foot shaft beneath it, into a kettle of water.
